title: Design a Direct Message Delivery Platform
prompt:
Design a direct-message service for pairs of users. A sender needs a durable acknowledgement, recipients may be offline or connected from multiple devices, and each conversation must present messages in one consistent order. Clients may retry after a timeout, reconnect from a stored cursor, and receive a live message and replayed message more than once.

Define the delivery, ordering, read-state, and presence contracts before choosing storage. Cover authorization, idempotency, sequence allocation, connection routing, offline replay, attachments, retention, failover, abuse controls, and observability. Explain which parts are strongly consistent and which are allowed to be stale.

Do not turn presence into a message-delivery guarantee or claim that a successful socket write proves a recipient read a message.

response.placeholder: Decide exactly when a send becomes durable, then define a conversation sequence that works for both live delivery and replay.
response.reference_answer:
## Contract

A send is acknowledged only after sender authorization, idempotency registration, allocation of a conversation sequence, and durable message persistence succeed. One direct conversation has a total order by sequence; there is no global order across conversations. A client retry with the same client message ID returns the same accepted message and sequence. Delivery is at least once, while the client makes duplicates harmless with message ID and conversation sequence.

## Durable write and ordering

Store conversation membership separately from messages. Route writes for one conversation to one logical sequencer or a transactionally protected sequence allocator. The durable transition records `(conversation_id, sender_id, client_message_id)`, message metadata, sequence, and an outbox event. A new owner uses a lease epoch and recovers from the committed message position; a stale owner cannot assign or publish a later sequence.

## Live delivery and offline replay

Gateways own ephemeral socket connections only. A short-lived connection registry provides delivery hints to gateways, but durable conversation history is the repair path. Each device reports its highest contiguous applied sequence. On reconnect it requests the gap from the durable API; a live socket message and replay can arrive twice without changing state. Bounded connection buffers protect gateways: a slow device is told to resynchronize rather than accumulating unlimited queued messages.

## Attachments, read state, and presence

Attachments upload directly to object storage through a scoped, short-lived grant. The message references immutable attachment metadata only after verification and policy checks. Read position is a monotonic per-user/per-conversation cursor and may be asynchronously updated. Presence uses expiring heartbeats and is explicitly approximate; it neither authorizes a send nor proves delivery or read.

## Security and operations

Authorize membership on every send and history read, enforce sender and attachment quotas, and retain audit records for moderation. Encrypt data in transit and at rest, use opaque object identifiers, and define retention/deletion behavior for both message metadata and bytes. Monitor durable-send latency, sequencer conflicts, idempotency hits, outbox lag, replay volume, socket backlog, gap repairs, owner failover, abuse rejects, and attachment verification failures.

## Progressive Hints

1. Give each conversation one authoritative sequence.
2. A live push is an optimization, not the source of truth.
3. A retry key must survive a gateway crash.
4. Treat read receipts and presence as separate state machines.
